references.text: The elders of Gilead ask Jephthah to become their leader and fight against the Ammonites, which is the direct fulfillment of the promise given in 10:18.
Jephthah is made head over all the inhabitants of Gilead, as was promised in 10:18.
Jephthah judged Israel for six years, showing that he became the leader over Gilead who was promised.
The people of Israel ask Samuel for a king who can go out before them and lead their wars, similar to the need for a military leader in Gilead.
The promise that whoever kills Goliath will become great in Israel is similar to the promise of leadership to whoever fights against the Ammonites.
Israel's earlier victory over the Amorites under Moses shows that Gilead was Israelite territory that now had to be defended against the Ammonites.
